response.sql: WITH site_stats AS (SELECT s.entrystat, sp.zoneref, AVG(sp.memusagegb) AS avg_ram, AVG(CASE WHEN sp.proccpu <> 0 THEN sp.procgpu * 1.0 / sp.proccpu END) AS avg_ratio FROM scanprocessing sp JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = sp.zoneref WHERE sp.memusagegb >= 60.8 AND s.entrystat IS NOT NULL GROUP BY s.entrystat, sp.zoneref) SELECT entrystat AS access_status, AVG(avg_ram) AS avg_of_site_ram, AVG(avg_ratio) AS avg_of_site_gpu_cpu_ratio FROM site_stats GROUP BY entrystat;

assumptions.assumption: The cutoff is inclusive: runs with memusagegb >= 60.8 count as memory-heavy.
Runs are linked to sites by scanprocessing.zoneref = sites.zoneregistry, with an inner join so runs without a matching site are dropped.
Missing values are ignored: NULL memusagegb rows fall out of the cutoff filter, and the GPU/CPU ratio skips rows where procgpu or proccpu is NULL or proccpu is 0.
Runs whose site has a NULL entrystat are excluded, since the request says to ignore missing values.
Each site counts equally in the final averages: the per-site averages are computed first, then averaged across sites within each access status.
The ratio uses 1.0 multiplication so it is computed as a true division rather than integer division. The SQL targets a PostgreSQL-style dialect.

alternatives.interpretation: The cutoff is strict: only runs with memory usage strictly greater than 60.8 GB count as memory-heavy.
